title: THIRD PARTY IN MARRIAGE
mv: Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
mvp: “Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” Ecclesiastes 4:12 (NKJV)
assignment: List five (5) potential third parties (people or structure) that could impact your marriage negatively if not well managed (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: Third party in a marriage relationship refers to the presence or inclusion of a third person in the couple’s life. The matter of a third party in marriage has been a controversial and debated issue. Many couples were advised to avoid third parties even before entering their marriage because of negative influences. However there is a need for a third party inclusion that can help navigate difficult and challenging phases in marriage (Proverbs 11:14; Proverbs 27:17).

It is not a sign of weakness to seek help in marriage when it is needed. Rather, it is a sign of intelligence to show that you know your capabilities and limits. The categories of people that can add value to your marriage include:

i: Spiritual Counsellors: Spiritual marriage counsellors often use techniques like prayer, meditation or discussions about spiritual texts that resonate with the couple’s beliefs to help address their challenges and strengthen their relationship.

Parents: Couples with marital issues may seek help from their parents when it is obvious that they cannot handle it on their own. A good example is, abuse. However, caution must be taken to avoid complications by ungodly Parents (Proverbs 4:1-4; 11:14).

A licensed marriage and family therapist: These professionals are important third parties to engage in marriage. They use their wealth of knowledge and experience to guide in handling conflicts correctly (Proverbs 15:22).

Trusted professionals in legal or family matters: When specific legal issues or financial structures are involved, choose someone who is neutral and can offer objective advice, not someone who is biased (Proverbs 24:6).
Mentors/Role models: These are people you look up to in marital affairs and they are usually from people around you who are either experienced or knowledgeable in this field.

b.x: Caution must however be exercised in understanding the potentials of anyone called to help in your marriage. Be sure you know the character, beliefs of such on marriage and general outlook on life, watch out for negative influence and opt out as soon as possible.

The Scriptures teach that Jesus Christ should be involved in every aspect of our lives including marital (1 Corinthians 11:3; Colossians 1:18). The presence of Jesus in the marriage gives couples a shoulder they can lean on (Proverbs 3:5). He can bring miracles into your marriage (John 2:1-12). The insight of Jesus on marriage can help to navigate challenges (Matthew 19:1-12).

With Jesus in the marriage, couples know exactly what to do per time and His presence brings joy and healing (Psalm 16:11; Matthew 8:14-15); A marriage centred on God creates a spiritual foundation that encourages both partners to seek divine guidance in their relationship (Psalm 32:8). Ecclesiastes 4:12 emphasises the strength of a threefold cord, suggesting that a marriage involving God is less likely to break under pressure. Involving God through prayers helps to provide guidance to navigate conflicts with a spirit of forgiveness and understanding (James 1:5; Proverbs 3:5-6).
Jesus is the ultimate third party in a marriage relationship, involve Him.
